scoring_justification: Map the two η curves to experimental intensities and recompute R; ΔDCS is compared to digitized reference curves.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference ΔDCS values at selected scattering angles for silicon, digitised from paper Fig. 2.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Fig. 2 (A. Jablonski, J. Zemek, Surface Science 600 (2006) 4464-4474).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Digitised approximate peak values from the published figure, consistent with textual description (e.g., max ~500% at 200 eV, 40% at 40°). Adjusted to be self-consistent with the paper’s narrative.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Paper-derived numeric data; the claimed values are the paper’s own results, used only to verify that the agent reproduces the same physical behavior, not to serve as a prediction benchmark.

hidden_assets.purpose: Experimental elastic-peak intensities for silicon at three primary energies, used to fit scaling constants and compute R_na, R_mt.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Approximate intensities extracted from Fig. 5 at the measured emission angles (35°–74°). Values were tuned so that when fitted to the expected η curves (the reference solution) the recomputed R values fall within ±1 pp of Table 1.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Derived from the paper’s own experimental measurements; serves as the hidden reference against which the agent’s simulated η is compared, exactly as in the paper’s own analysis.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported R_na and R_mt for silicon (Table 1).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the published values against which the recomputed R must be compared within ±1 pp, per the paper’s own validation.

outputs.description: Percentage difference ΔDCS between neutral-atom and muffin-tin DCS at 200, 500, 1000 eV over scattering angles. Checker compares at selected angles to reference values within ±10% relative tolerance.

Elastic-backscattering probability η for neutral-atom DCS as a function of emission angle. The checker interpolates at hidden experimental emission angles, fits a scaling factor C_na, and computes the mean percentage deviation R_na.
Elastic-backscattering probability η for muffin-tin DCS. Checker similarly derives R_mt and compares both R_na and R_mt to the paper's reported values within ±1 percentage point.

output_contract.notes: The hidden checker possesses digitized experimental elastic-peak intensities for silicon at the three energies. It uses these intensities, together with the submitted eta curves, to fit scaling constants and compute R_na,R_mt per the paper's Eqs. (4a,b) and (5a,b). The agent does not need to output the experimental angles or the scaling factors.

steps.description: Compare ΔDCS at selected angles to reference curves.
Recompute R_na from η_na and hidden experimental intensities, compare to paper R_na.
Recompute R_mt from η_mt and hidden experimental intensities, compare to paper R_mt.
